provenance.source: NVIDIA Vera Rubin roadmap disclosure (GTC 2025 + CES 2026 announcements). HBM4 vendor target; 2H 2026 shipping target.
provenance.notes: Roadmap claim — every figure on this component is a vendor target until silicon ships. AMD MI455X claims 432 GB HBM4 (50% more) — the memory-capacity-AMD-lead pattern from current gen REPEATS at the roadmap pair.

provenance.source: NVIDIA Vera Rubin bandwidth target — bumped from ~13 TB/s at GTC 2025 to ~22 TB/s at CES 2026 in an explicit competitive response to AMD MI455X positioning. Cite the GTC 2025 → CES 2026 announcement sequence.
provenance.notes: COMPETITIVE-RESPONSE STORY: the ~22 TB/s figure is a chosen-late spec, NOT an organic generation step. NVIDIA raised the bandwidth target between GTC 2025 and CES 2026 to land above MI455X's claimed 19.6 TB/s. The bandwidth lead is real (per current claims) AND tactically positioned — surface both readings.

range.unit: PFLOPS (dense, RANGE — spread across public disclosures)

provenance.source: NVIDIA Vera Rubin FP4 figures vary across public disclosures by dense/sparse and per-GPU framing. Range 35-50 PFLOPS captures the spread honestly rather than asserting a single point. AMD MI455X claims 40 PFLOPS FP4 — sits INSIDE the NVIDIA spread, so no defensible winner.
provenance.notes: Rendered as a RANGE on purpose — public disclosures conflict on dense/sparse attribution and per-GPU framing. The spread IS the honest signal. AMD's 40 PFLOPS claim lies inside the range — UNRESOLVED is the correct verdict, not a winner.

compute_flops_fp8_per_gpu_dense.text: ~3.5× Blackwell B200 (vendor multiplier, no point figure — Blackwell FP8 base is itself verify-needed)

provenance.source: NVIDIA Vera Rubin FP8 is described as a multiplier (~3.5×) on Blackwell B200 FP8. Blackwell FP8 dense is itself a verify-needed datasheet read (~9 PFLOPS dense, approx). A multiplier on a verify-needed base = double-uncertainty; no defensible point value to compare against AMD MI455X's 20 PFLOPS claim.
provenance.notes: LAYERED UNCERTAINTY: vendor multiplier on a verify-needed base. UNRESOLVED is the honest verdict — neither PARITY (asserts confidence we don't have) nor a clean lead (no firm Rubin number to compare). Distinct from FP4's overlapping-range UNRESOLVED — FP8 has no firm Rubin figure at all.

provenance.notes: Customer-archetype framing. Quantum-X800 buyers prioritize collective-op performance and SHARP in-network compute over Ethernet's ecosystem fit; distinct from Spectrum-X's Ethernet integration story but both are NVIDIA-integrated.

software_tensorrt_llm_availability.text: NVIDIA-only — does not run on AMD ROCm

provenance.source: TensorRT-LLM is a CUDA-only library by design; ROCm has no compatible re-implementation as of writing.

software_framework_support.text: PyTorch (CUDA-native), TensorFlow, JAX, vLLM, SGLang, MLX — full first-class support across all major ML frameworks. CUDA-native at the kernel level. Most new frameworks ship CUDA-first in their primary release path.

provenance.source: NVIDIA CUDA + NVAIE product materials confirm first-class CUDA support across major ML frameworks; CUDA-first default in framework release paths is widely documented in PyTorch / TF / vLLM release notes.

software_mainstream_inference.text: Baseline (100%) — H100 + Blackwell are NVIDIA's own silicon. Mainstream PyTorch / vLLM throughput on NVIDIA is the reference point against which all competitors are measured.

provenance.source: NVIDIA is the baseline by construction — competitor benchmarks express their throughput as a fraction of (or beat of) H100 / Blackwell. Not a vendor claim; an artifact of how the industry measures inference performance.

software_cuda_exclusive_libs.text: TensorRT-LLM (CUDA-only, no ROCm port planned), FlashAttention 3 (CUDA-only as of 2026; ROCm has FlashAttention 2 via Triton for RDNA3 but not FA3 — missing FA3 reportedly costs 30-40% training throughput on 7B+ models per Spheron May 2026), NCCL collective communication (no ROCm equivalent), cuDNN, cuBLAS, Triton inference server — the library moat.

provenance.source: TensorRT-LLM CUDA-only confirmed by NVIDIA TensorRT documentation + multiple 2026 analyses (Spheron, Thundercompute). FlashAttention 3 ROCm gap quantified in Spheron May 2026 (30-40% training throughput cost at 7B+ models). NCCL has no ROCm equivalent per AMD ROCm compatibility docs.
provenance.notes: Library moat is real, specific, and named. Workloads using TensorRT-LLM or FA3 stay on CUDA today; workloads on stock PyTorch / vLLM can move to ROCm but at variable performance cost.

software_ecosystem_maturity.text: ~20 years of CUDA ecosystem (released 2007). cuDNN, cuBLAS, TensorRT, NCCL, Triton inference server, NeMo, NIM. Compounding ecosystem moat: more libraries, more courses, more papers, more practitioner-hours, more tooling defaults. CUDA-first default for new research and ML infrastructure.

provenance.source: CUDA's ecosystem age (release year 2007) + library breadth + community size are documented across analyst reports + practitioner surveys. 'CUDA-first default' characterization is directional — no single measured KPI captures 'ecosystem maturity.'

software_switching_cost.text: High — CUDA-native codebases require port effort to alternatives; CUDA-exclusive libs (TensorRT-LLM, FA3, NCCL) have no full equivalent — porting requires re-implementation or accepting performance penalties; CUDA-first tooling default means new work tends to come up on CUDA first, perpetuating the gap.

provenance.source: Switching cost synthesized from practitioner reports of CUDA -> ROCm porting + analyst coverage (Spheron 2026, SemiAnalysis, Thundercompute 2026). Not a measured single number.
